The Result Clause
You can talk about the results of an action by using a result clause. There are several ways that you can do this both in speaking and writing.
I never have the right ingredients in my kitchen, and consequently, I eat too much fast food.
If you want to talk about a result, you can use:
You need to make sure that you always have the basics in your kitchen so that you can make a quick and healthy meal with just a few fresh ingredients.
It looks so easy that even I could make it.
These are such good recipes that I've served them all in the restaurant.
You're going to have to throw caution to the wind and try some new things; otherwise, you'll be stuck in a rut.
No arguing or else you won't make it through the month.

Unlikely Conditionals: Would in the If-Clause

You can use the second conditional to talk about unlikely conditions. In this conditional, you use would in the main clause.
You can also use would in the if-clause, but the meaning of the sentence would be that of a polite request.
If you would both pick a few recipes, we could make a shopping list.

You can use would in the if-clause to express requests or ask politely for someone to do something.

Unlikely Conditional:
If I had more money, I would buy more expensive clothing.
Polite Request:
If you would please wait here, the doctor will be in soon.
If you would help me with my homework, I could understand the lesson more easily.
If you would just look at it, you would see that it's healthy and sounds really tasty.
If you would take a little more time to look, we could find something more interesting.
If you would just try them in some recipes, I think you would change your mind.

Vanessa: Okay, if you would both pick a few recipes, we could make a shopping list. You need to make sure that you always have the basics in your kitchen so that you can make a quick and healthy meal with just a few fresh ingredients. A big mistake that many people make is not having basic spices and base ingredients to cook with. That's when you end up ordering take out food or picking up fast food on the way home.
Peter: Yes. I never have the right ingredients in my kitchen, and consequently, I eat too much fast food.
Vanessa: So, let's look at a couple recipes. You two can pick some that sound interesting and delicious!

Amy: How about this? Vegetable broth soup? It looks so easy that I could even make it.
Peter: Broth? Sounds boring!
Amy: Peter, if you would just look at it, you would see that it's healthy and sounds really tasty.
Peter: Amy, if you would take a little more time to look, we could find something more interesting.
Vanessa: Okay you two. No arguing or else you won't make it through the month. These are such good recipes that I've served them all in the restaurant.
Peter: Lentil and sweet potato stew? No thanks. I hate lentils. This recipe is out!

Vanessa: Lentils are so good for you though. If you would just try them in some recipes I think you would change your mind.
Amy: I'll make the lentil recipe. You can try a bit Peter, to see if you like it. You're gonna have to throw caution to the wind and try some new things; otherwise, you'll be stuck in a rut. Try to be a little bit more broad-minded.
Vanessa: Okay, are we ready to go to the supermarket?
